title: Coherent Duality on Projective Cohen-Macaulay Schemes

items.title: Dualizing complexes and the normalized dualizing sheaf on a projective CM scheme
items.statement: A dualizing complex on a Noetherian scheme is a bounded coherent complex that locally has finite injective dimension and satisfies the homothety isomorphism; over a field a normalization adds a trace with the evaluation isomorphisms, and the normalized dualizing sheaf of a pure d-dimensional CM scheme is omega_X = H^{-d}(D_X).
items.strategy: The definition fixes the local conditions, the shift convention and the normalized representation used by every later item; no existence or uniqueness is asserted here.

items.title: Derived adjunction for finite rings and closed immersions
items.statement: Assume AC. For a finite map A->B of Noetherian rings, R Hom_A(B,G) is right adjoint to restriction of scalars; for a closed immersion i:X->Y, i^!G = i^{-1}R Hom_Y(i_*O_X,G) is right adjoint to i_* in internal and global derived Hom, with counit evaluation at 1, and R Gamma(Y,i_*K) = R Gamma(X,K).
items.strategy: Give the evaluation-at-1 adjunction on rings, show coinduction preserves injectives, transfer to a closed immersion by the same formula, and finish with flasque resolutions for the cohomology comparison.

items.title: Dualizing complexes and coherent biduality for regular-ring quotients
items.statement: Assume AC. For a regular Noetherian ring A of finite dimension, an invertible A-module L, and B=A/I nonzero, R Hom_A(B,L[s]) is a dualizing complex over B for every s, and coherent derived biduality holds for objects of D^b_fin(B); the assertions localize.
items.strategy: Use finite projective resolutions and ambient double duality over A, then the finite-map coinduction adjunction to descend biduality to B and identify the homothety map.

items.title: Ext concentration for a Cohen-Macaulay quotient of a regular local ring
items.statement: Assume AC. If R is the localization of a polynomial ring over a field at a maximal ideal, of dimension N, and B=R/I is Cohen-Macaulay of dimension d, then Ext_R^q(B,R)=0 for q != N-d, and the same holds with an invertible R-module in place of R.
items.strategy: Auslander-Buchsbaum gives pd_R B=N-d for q>c; prime avoidance constructs a length-c regular sequence inside I, verifying each new element is a parameter using dimension and minimal parameter length before invoking the qualified CM quotient theorem; derived adjunction shifts Ext to negative degrees for q<c.

items.title: Existence and biduality from a projective embedding
items.statement: Assume AC. For X projective over a field with closed embedding i into P^N, D_i = i^!(omega_P[N]) is a dualizing complex; every bounded coherent K satisfies K = D_i D_i(K) via canonical evaluation, with no smoothness or CM hypothesis.
items.strategy: Resolve omega_P[N] injectively and apply the closed-immersion coinduction; on each regular affine chart the regular-quotient lemma gives the local dualizing conditions and biduality, and the charts cover X.

items.title: Derived coherent duality on projective space
items.statement: Assume AC. On P^N, evaluation composed with the Laurent residue trace gives a natural quasi-isomorphism R Gamma(R Hom_P(K,omega_P[N])) -> R Hom_k(R Gamma(P,K),k) for every bounded coherent K, compatible with shifts and triangles.
items.strategy: Check the map on twists and finite direct sums using the twisting cohomology and residue pairing, then extend to bounded coherent complexes through finite locally free resolutions and the long exact sequences of a triangle.

items.title: Normalized trace and independence of a projective embedding
items.statement: Assume AC. The embedding dualizing complex D_i carries a trace t_i to k inducing Hom_{D(X)}(K,D_i[r]) = Hom_k(H^{-r}(X,K),k); two embeddings give a unique trace-preserving isomorphism, defining the normalized D_X.
items.strategy: Identify the pairing with the ambient evaluation trace, then apply the Yoneda evaluation bijection to compare the two representing objects on bounded coherent complexes.

items.title: Concentration of the projective dualizing complex on a pure CM scheme
items.statement: Assume AC. If X is projective over a field, Cohen-Macaulay and pure of dimension d, then D_X = omega_X[d] with omega_X = H^{-d}(D_X); for an embedding into P^N, i_*omega_X = Ext_P^{N-d}(i_*O_X,omega_P), and omega_X is coherent, CM and has support X.
items.strategy: Local Ext concentration at closed points gives the single surviving degree, which spreads by coherence; the dual of a finite free resolution then shows omega_X is CM with full support.

items.title: Serre duality for coherent sheaves on a projective Cohen-Macaulay scheme
items.statement: Assume AC. For X projective, pure d-dimensional and Cohen-Macaulay over a field, every coherent F satisfies a natural perfect pairing Ext_X^{d-i}(F,omega_X) x H^i(X,F) -> H^d(X,omega_X) -> k, equivalently Ext_X^{d-i}(F,omega_X) = H^i(X,F)^dual; the complex form is R Hom_X(K,D_X) = R Hom_k(R Gamma(X,K),k) with coherent derived biduality.
items.strategy: Specialize the normalized embedding duality to r=-i and D_X=omega_X[d], identify Yoneda classes with cohomology, and use finite-dimensionality of coherent cohomology to make both adjoints of the pairing isomorphisms.
items.proof_strategy:
Complete current local proof:
1.1 Apply [F1] to $F$ with $r=-i$. Since $D_X=\omega_X[d]$ by [F2], its left side becomes $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(F,\omega_X[d-i])=\operatorname{Ext}_X^{d-i}(F,\omega_X)$; its right side is $\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^i(X,F),k)$. For $\eta\in H^i(X,F)$, [F3] represents it by $\beta:\mathcal O_X\to F[i]$. A class $\alpha:F\to\omega_X[d-i]$ pairs with it by $t_X(\alpha[i]\circ\beta)$. This is the Yoneda composition of [F3] and is exactly the evaluation comparison proved in [F1]. Thus it is bilinear, natural in $F$, and compatible with shifts and connecting maps. [F1, F2, F3, construct]

2.1 Apply [F4] to the closed subscheme $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^N_k$ supplied by a projective embedding: its finite-dimensionality clause gives that each $H^i(X,F)$ is a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space. The isomorphism in step 1.1 proves that the adjoint map from Ext to the dual of cohomology is an isomorphism. For a finite-dimensional space, evaluation into its double dual is an isomorphism, so the other adjoint map is an isomorphism as well. Outside $0\le i\le d$, cohomology vanishes by [F4] and the negative-degree convention; step 1.1 then proves the corresponding Ext vanishing. For bounded coherent $K$, retain the actual global derived comparison used in [F1]: closed-immersion adjunction gives $R\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,D_X)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_P(i_*K,\omega_P[N])$, and the projective-space evaluation/trace map identifies the latter with $R\operatorname{Hom}_k(R\Gamma(P,i_*K),k)=R\operatorname{Hom}_k(R\Gamma(X,K),k)$. This comparison is an isomorphism in $D(k)$ induced by the same counit and trace, so its naturality and signs are those of [F1]. The biduality $K\cong\mathcal R\!Hom_X(\mathcal R\!Hom_X(K,D_X),D_X)$ is the coherent biduality of the embedding construction [F1], valid after pushing into the ambient projective space, without imposing perfectness on $K$ over the singular scheme. AC enters through the cited resolution, derived-composition and cohomology suppliers. [F1, F4, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: The smooth projective locally free theorem is the special case
items.statement: Under AC, for smooth projective X the coherent theorem specializes: omega_X is the canonical line bundle, R Hom(E,omega_X)=E^dual tensor omega_X for finite locally free E, and the pairing recovers the published AG-LIE locally free theorem with the same trace.
items.strategy: Identify the canonical line by regular-immersion Koszul and conormal adjunction, and transport the coherent counit trace through the normalized collapse sigma_c=(-1)^(c(c+1)/2) exactly once; published Gysin compatibility recovers the smooth pairing.

items.title: Curve duality and its residue normalization in dimension one
items.statement: Under AC, the d=1 case gives H^1(C,F)^dual = Hom_C(F,omega_C) and H^0(C,F)^dual = Ext_C^1(F,omega_C) for coherent F on a projective pure CM curve, including singular curves; for smooth C and vector bundles it recovers the residue-normalized curve pairing.
items.strategy: Specialize the theorem to d=1 and identify the trace normalization with the point Koszul residue classes, which determine the trace on every component.

title: Coherent Duality on Projective Cohen-Macaulay Schemes — Examples

items.title: Coherent duality on a singular plane cubic
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the nodal cubic C: y^2 z = x^2(x+z) has omega_C = O_C; the trace pairs H^1(C,O_C)=k with H^0(C,omega_C)=k, and at the node Ext_C^1(k_p,omega_C)=k while Hom_C(k_p,omega_C)=0.
items.strategy: Establish integrality and the node, verify the hypersurface equation is a regular parameter locally before using the CM quotient theorem, dualize the cubic structure sequence to compute omega_C and cohomology, and apply the A theorem to the structure sheaf and node skyscraper.

items.title: Surface duality for twists and a skyscraper on the projective plane
items.statement: On P^2 over a field, omega=O(-3): for m>=0 duality pairs the binomial number of monomials in H^0(O(m)) with H^2(O(-m-3)) via the Laurent coefficient pairing, and at a rational point Ext^2(k_p,omega)=k while Ext^1(k_p,omega)=Hom(k_p,omega)=0.
items.strategy: Identify omega and the pairing on P^2 from the smooth specialization and the residue pairing, then apply the A-page theorem to the point skyscraper.

items.title: The affine line disproves the proper duality formula without properness
items.statement: The coherent duality formula without the properness hypothesis fails on the smooth affine line: H^1(A^1,O)=0 while Ext^0(O,Omega^1)=k[t]dt is nonzero, so the degree-one pairing cannot be the asserted duality.
items.strategy: Use affine vanishing for the left side and the nonzero global sections of the Kaehler differentials on the right, after checking the nonclosed image of the projection witnessing nonproperness.
